subject: pe
title: Stretch: Long-Term Adaptations
welcome_lead: Stretch your knowledge — how does the body adapt after months of training?
meta_desc: GCSE PE stretch: long-term anatomy and physiology adaptations to training.
final_note: Top work! You understand how the body transforms with consistent training.

concepts.def: Increase in muscle size from resistance training.
Enlargement of the heart muscle from training.
Resting heart rate below 60 bpm, common in athletes.
Growth of more capillaries around muscles and alveoli.
Mass of mineral per unit of bone volume.
Maximum air exhaled after a maximum inhalation.

walkthroughs.body_html: Resistance training causes hypertrophy — fibres thicken and strengthen. Tendons and ligaments also strengthen, reducing injury risk. Weight-bearing exercise increases bone density, protecting against osteoporosis later in life.

Endurance training produces cardiac hypertrophy — a larger, stronger heart with greater stroke volume. Resting heart rate falls, sometimes below 60 bpm, called bradycardia. Cardiac output at rest stays similar.
Training increases vital capacity and improves gas exchange through capillarisation around alveoli and muscles. More red blood cells boost oxygen transport, raising VO2 max.
